title: CBSE CLASS 9 — Biology | Mutations Genetic Disorders
description: Subject-wise test on Mutations Genetic Disorders (Biology) for CBSE CLASS 9. 25Q.
subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following terms describes the passing of traits from parents to offspring?

options.explanation: Adaptation refers to the process of becoming better suited to the environment.
Evolution is the process of change in the genetic makeup of a population over time.
Heredity is the passing of traits from parents to offspring.
Mutation is a sudden, heritable change in the genetic material of an organism.

questions.explanation: Heredity is the process by which characteristics are transmitted from one generation to the next.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: A sudden, heritable change in the genetic material of an organism is called a:

options.explanation: Variation refers to differences among individuals, which can arise from mutations, sexual reproduction, etc.
Mutation is a sudden, heritable change in the genetic material of an organism.
Adaptation refers to the process of becoming better suited to the environment.
Trait refers to a characteristic or quality of an organism.

questions.explanation: A mutation is a permanent, heritable change in the DNA sequence.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a genetic disorder?

options.explanation: Dengue fever is an infectious disease.
Tuberculosis is an infectious disease.
Hemophilia is an inherited genetic disorder.
Malaria is an infectious disease.

questions.explanation: Hemophilia is an inherited genetic disorder that impairs the body's ability to make blood clots.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Variations arising during the process of reproduction can be beneficial, harmful, or neutral. Which of the following is the primary source of these variations?

options.explanation: Environmental factors can influence the expression of traits but are not the primary source of heritable variation.
Lifestyle choices can influence the expression of traits but are not the primary source of heritable variation.
Changes in genetic material are the primary source of heritable variation.
Dietary habits can influence the expression of traits but are not the primary source of heritable variation.

questions.explanation: Variations are primarily caused by changes in the genetic material (DNA), such as through mutations or recombination during sexual reproduction.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: If a genetic disorder is passed down from parents to their child, it means the disorder is:

options.explanation: Acquired disorders develop during a person's lifetime due to environmental factors or lifestyle, and are not passed genetically.
Inherited disorders are passed down through genes from parents to their offspring.
Infectious disorders are caused by the spread of diseases.
Contagious disorders are caused by the spread of diseases.

questions.explanation: Inherited disorders are those that are passed down through genes from parents to their offspring.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: A new trait appears in an offspring that was not present in either parent. This could be a result of:

options.explanation: Environmental influence can affect the expression of traits but is unlikely to introduce a completely new trait.
Adaptation to new surroundings can affect the expression of traits but is unlikely to introduce a completely new trait.

options.text: A new mutation in the offspring
options.explanation: A new mutation in the offspring is the most likely explanation for a new trait that was not present in either parent.

options.text: A dominant gene from one parent
options.explanation: A dominant gene from one parent would express a trait already present in one of the parents, not introduce a completely new trait.

questions.explanation: If a trait is entirely new and not present in either parent, it is most likely due to a new mutation occurring in the germ cells of the parents or in the early developmental stages of the offspring.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which component of the cell carries the genetic information that determines an organism's traits?

options.explanation: DNA carries the genetic information that determines an organism's traits.
Proteins are molecules that perform a variety of functions in the cell, but they do not carry genetic information.
Lipids are molecules that serve as energy storage and structural components of the cell, but they do not carry genetic information.
Carbohydrates are molecules that serve as energy sources and structural components of the cell, but they do not carry genetic information.

questions.explanation: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is the molecule that carries the genetic instructions used in the growth, development, functioning, and reproduction of all known organisms.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Consider a scenario where a population of bacteria is exposed to an antibiotic. Most bacteria die, but a few survive and reproduce, leading to a new population resistant to the antibiotic. This phenomenon is best explained by:

options.explanation: Acquired immunity refers to the immune system's ability to recognize and respond to pathogens, but it does not explain the development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
Pre-existing genetic mutations in a few individuals within the population can lead to antibiotic resistance.
Environmental adaptation can contribute to the development of antibiotic resistance, but it is not the primary explanation for this phenomenon.
Behavioral changes do not explain the development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria.

questions.explanation: Antibiotic resistance in bacteria usually arises from pre-existing genetic mutations in a few individuals within the population.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): All mutations are harmful to an organism. Reason (R): Mutations always lead to severe genetic disorders.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

options.text: Both A and R are false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are false. Not all mutations are harmful; some can be neutral or even beneficial.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: A family has three children. The eldest child has blue eyes, the middle child has brown eyes (like both parents), and the youngest child also has blue eyes. Based on this observation, which statement about eye color inheritance is most likely true?

options.text: Brown eye color is a recessive trait.
options.explanation: Brown eye color is typically dominant over blue eye color.

options.text: Blue eye color is an acquired trait.
options.explanation: Blue eye color is an inherited trait, not an acquired one.

options.text: Both parents carry genes for blue eye color.
options.explanation: Both parents must carry the gene for blue eyes to produce children with blue eyes.

options.text: The youngest child's blue eyes are due to a new mutation.
options.explanation: It is less likely that the youngest child's blue eyes are due to a new mutation when a simpler genetic explanation (recessive inheritance) fits.

questions.explanation: If both parents have brown eyes but produce children with blue eyes, it implies that both parents must carry the gene for blue eyes.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following refers to a sudden, heritable change in the genetic material of an organism?

options.explanation: Adaptation is a process of adjusting to the environment.
Variation refers to differences among individuals.
A mutation is a sudden, random, and heritable change in the DNA sequence or chromosome structure of an organism.
Evolution is the change in heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations.

questions.explanation: A mutation is defined as a sudden, random, and heritable change in the DNA sequence or chromosome structure of an organism.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an agent that can cause mutations?

options.explanation: Water is generally not considered a direct mutagen.
Visible sunlight is generally not considered a direct mutagen in the typical context.
X-rays are a type of ionizing radiation known to cause damage to DNA, leading to mutations.
Oxygen is generally not considered a direct mutagen in the typical context.

questions.explanation: X-rays are a type of ionizing radiation known to cause damage to DNA, leading to mutations.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: A genetic disorder is primarily caused by:

options.explanation: Bacterial infections cause infectious diseases, not genetic disorders.
Viral infections cause infectious diseases, not genetic disorders.

options.text: An abnormality in an individual's DNA
options.explanation: Genetic disorders are conditions caused by changes or abnormalities in an individual's DNA.
Nutritional deficiencies cause deficiency diseases, not genetic disorders.

questions.explanation: Genetic disorders are conditions caused by changes or abnormalities in an individual's DNA.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): All variations in a species are beneficial for its survival. Reason (R): Mutations are the ultimate source of all variations.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is false, so this option cannot be correct.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is false, so this option cannot be correct.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because not all variations are beneficial, but Reason (R) is true because mutations are the source of variations.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is true, so this option cannot be correct.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because not all variations are beneficial; some can be harmful or neutral. Reason (R) is true because mutations are indeed the ultimate source of new genetic variations.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Consider a trait like eye color in humans. If a child has blue eyes, while both parents have brown eyes, this difference is an example of:

options.explanation: An acquired trait is developed during an organism's lifetime due to environmental influences or activities.
Environmental influences do not directly determine eye color in this context.
The child's blue eyes are a result of genetic inheritance, as both parents can be carriers of the recessive gene for blue eyes.

options.text: Mutation leading to a new trait
options.explanation: While a new mutation could cause a new trait, this scenario is more about the expression of existing genetic variation.

questions.explanation: Eye color is a genetically determined trait, and the scenario described is a common example of genetic variation and inheritance.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about genetic disorders is most accurate for Class 9?

options.text: All genetic disorders are always visible at birth.
options.explanation: Not all genetic disorders are visible at birth; some may manifest later in life.

options.text: Genetic disorders can only be inherited from parents.
options.explanation: Some genetic disorders can arise from new mutations in the individual, not just from inheritance.

options.text: Genetic disorders result from changes in the genetic material.
options.explanation: Genetic disorders are fundamentally caused by alterations in DNA.

options.text: Genetic disorders can be cured by antibiotics.
options.explanation: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not genetic disorders.

questions.explanation: Genetic disorders result from changes in the genetic material.

questions.question: A genetic disorder known as Down syndrome is caused by the presence of an extra copy of chromosome 21. This condition is an example of a disorder arising from a change in:

options.explanation: Down syndrome is not caused by a change in a single gene sequence but by an extra chromosome.
Down syndrome is a genetic condition, not caused by environmental factors.
Down syndrome is caused by having an extra copy of chromosome 21, which is a change in chromosome number.
Down syndrome is a genetic condition, not caused by a viral infection.

questions.explanation: Down syndrome is characterized by trisomy 21, meaning there are three copies of chromosome 21 instead of the usual two.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is most likely to be an *acquired* trait rather than an *inherited* trait?

options.explanation: Natural hair color is an inherited trait.
Blood group is an inherited trait.
A scar from an injury is an example of an acquired trait, developed after an environmental influence or activity.
Eye color is an inherited trait.

questions.explanation: Acquired traits are characteristics developed during an organism's lifetime due to environmental influences or activities.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: A child is diagnosed with a rare genetic disorder that was not present in either parent or any known relatives. What is the most probable cause of this disorder in the child?

options.text: It was acquired from a viral infection during pregnancy.
options.explanation: Viral infections do not typically cause genetic disorders in this manner.

options.text: It is an acquired trait developed after birth.
options.explanation: The question specifies it is a genetic disorder, not an acquired trait.

options.text: It resulted from a spontaneous new mutation in the child's germ cells or early development.
options.explanation: A spontaneous new mutation in the egg or sperm cell or very early in the child's development is the most probable cause of a genetic disorder not present in parents or relatives.

options.text: Both parents are carriers of the disorder, but it only expresses in offspring.
options.explanation: The question states the disorder was not present in parents or relatives, suggesting it is not an inherited condition from the parents.

questions.explanation: If a disorder is not present in parents or relatives, and it's a genetic disorder, the most probable cause is a spontaneous new mutation.
questions.subject: cbse9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of DNA in heredity?

options.text: DNA provides energy for cell functions.
options.explanation: DNA does not provide energy for cell functions; that role belongs to ATP and other energy molecules.

options.text: DNA helps in the synthesis of carbohydrates.
options.explanation: DNA's role is not directly in the synthesis of carbohydrates; it carries genetic information.

options.text: DNA carries genetic information from parents to offspring.
options.explanation: The primary role of DNA in heredity is to store and transmit genetic information from one generation to the next.

options.text: DNA is responsible for the movement of organelles within the cell.
options.explanation: DNA is not directly responsible for the movement of organelles within the cell; that is the role of the cytoskeleton and motor proteins.

questions.explanation: The primary role of DNA in heredity is to store and transmit genetic information from one generation to the next.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a mutation?

options.text: A sudden increase in an organism's size.
options.explanation: This describes a different biological phenomenon, not a mutation.

options.text: A change in an organism's behavior due to environmental factors.
options.explanation: This describes a change in behavior, not a genetic mutation.

options.text: A permanent alteration in the DNA sequence of an organism.
options.explanation: This is the correct definition of a mutation.

options.text: The process by which an organism adapts to its environment over generations.
options.explanation: This describes evolution or adaptation, not a mutation.

questions.explanation: A mutation is defined as a sudden, heritable change in the genetic material (DNA or RNA) of an organism.

questions.question: Genetic disorders are primarily caused by:

options.text: Poor nutrition and lack of exercise.
options.explanation: These are environmental factors that can influence health but are not primary causes of genetic disorders.
Infections can have genetic components but are not primary causes of genetic disorders.

options.text: Changes or errors in an individual's genetic material (DNA).
options.explanation: This is the primary cause of genetic disorders.
Environmental factors like weather conditions are not primary causes of genetic disorders.

questions.explanation: Genetic disorders arise from abnormalities in an individual's genome, which can be due to a single gene mutation, chromosome abnormalities, or multifactorial inheritance.

questions.question: Assertion (A): All mutations are harmful to an organism. Reason (R): Mutations introduce changes in the genetic code, which can alter protein function.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Assertion A is false, so this option cannot be correct.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Since A is false, this option is also incorrect.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Reason R is true, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: This is the correct assessment of the assertion and reason.

questions.question: What is the term for the agents that cause changes in the genetic material?

options.explanation: Antibodies are part of the immune system and do not cause genetic mutations.
Hormones are chemical messengers and do not typically cause genetic mutations.
This is the correct term for agents that cause genetic mutations.
Enzymes are biological catalysts and do not typically cause genetic mutations.

questions.explanation: Mutagens are physical or chemical agents that can cause changes or mutations in the genetic material (DNA or RNA) of an organism.

questions.question: A family notices that several members across generations suffer from a condition characterized by progressive muscle weakness and loss of muscle mass. This condition is more prevalent in males and seems to be passed down from mothers to their sons. This pattern strongly suggests that the condition is:

options.text: An infectious disease caused by a virus.
options.explanation: Infectious diseases do not typically follow the described inheritance pattern.

options.text: A nutritional deficiency that runs in the family.
options.explanation: Nutritional deficiencies do not have the specific inheritance pattern described.

options.text: A genetic disorder inherited through specific genes.
options.explanation: This is the correct assessment based on the description provided.

options.text: An allergic reaction to common environmental allergens.
options.explanation: Allergic reactions do not follow the described inheritance pattern and are not typically characterized by progressive muscle weakness.

questions.explanation: The description of the condition is characteristic of an inherited genetic disorder, specifically an X-linked recessive disorder.
